answer: Each identity docks at the jetty with a sponsor who locks a 90-credit bond in the marble ledger. A sponsor may back at most three per epoch, and one bond never covers two, so the thousandth fake needs its 90 credits and a slot. Auditors re-add the ledger each epoch; over quota or no entry loses bond and slot. Renting sponsors fails: rented slots count against the cap and the ledger exposes the star pattern. One thousand fakes need 334 sponsors and 90,000 credits; one honest agent needs 90 credits once. The lotus pass is single-use, bound to one key, so copying it creates no second identity.
